ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p38/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p38/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p38/r1.claim: The preposition after the verb gives the expression the force of a hasty assault; Pharaoh is already angry and may kill Moses and Aaron, plot against them, or become more rebellious before they can speak.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p38/r1.anchor: launching a hasty onslaught against someone

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p38/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p38/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p38/r2.claim: Moses and Aaron made the supplication together, showing that these directions came after Moses reached Egypt and Aaron joined him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p38/r2.anchor: In the supplication depicted in this verse

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r7.claim: The request concerns the psychological burden and anxiety of responsibility, not a physical speech defect; verse 28 asks that Moses's words be deeply understood, while both brothers feared the mission.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r7.anchor: onun kendisindeki fizyolojik bir ârızaya değil, üstlendiği görevin ağırlığı karşısında duyduğu sorumluluk duygusunun oluşturduğu psikolojik duruma ve bu konudaki endişelerine işaret etmek istediği anlaşılmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r9.claim: Moses had to persuade powerful people steeped in magic through rational proofs; the later signs before the people were meant to expose magic's baselessness, not serve as the core proofs of monotheism.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r9.anchor: büyünün ve göz boyama usullerinin çok revaçta olduğu bir toplumun ileri gelenlerini dahi akla ve idrak yeteneğine hitap eden delillerle ikna etme görevi üstlenmiş olduğunu

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r8.claim: Farata means to go ahead or precede; the related farit describes one who precedes a water party, and a leading horse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r8.anchor: فرط سبق وتقدم ومنه الفارط الذي يتقدم الواردة وفرس فرط تسبق الخيل انتهى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r9.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r9.claim: An unattributed poem uses farit for one who goes ahead of a party arriving at water, illustrating the lexical gloss.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r9.anchor: واستعجلونا وكانوا من صحابتنا ... كما تقدم فارط الوراد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r10.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r10.claim: A hadith has the Prophet say he will precede his community at the Pool; the phrase means he goes ahead of them.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r11.speaker: يحيى، أبو نوفل، وابن محيصن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r11.claim: Their passive reading of yufriṭ means that Pharaoh may outstrip them by hastening punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r11.anchor: وقرأ يحيى وأبو نوفل وابن محيصن في روايته أن يفرط مبنيا للمفعول أي يسبق في العقوبة ويسرع بها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r12.claim: The passive reading may also evoke excessive punishment, feared as something Satan, Pharaoh's arrogance, ambition, or rebellious Egyptians might spur him to inflict.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r12.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون من الإفراط ومجاوزة الحد في العقوبة خافا أن يحمله حامل على المعاجلة بالعذاب من شيطان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r13.speaker: فرقة والزعفراني عن ابن محيصن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r13.claim: Their yufriṭ reading with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on rāʾ means excessive harm or overstepping into improper speech; its open-ended wording is refined restraint.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r13.anchor: وقرأت فرقة والزعفراني عن ابن محيصن يفرط بضم الياء وكسر الراء من الإفراط في الأذية أو أن يطغى في التخطي إلى أن يقول فيك ما لا ينبغي

JISHUMI:v7p4672/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r5.claim: Prophets fear harm from their enemies until God reassures them.
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r5.anchor: وتدل على أن الأنبياء يخافون من شر أعدائهم حتى يؤمنهم الله تعالى.

ZAJJAJ:v3p358/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p358/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p358/r1.claim: Yafruṭ means to rush ahead to punish; related forms describe a matter happening early, excess, or falling short, all connected to advancing, since farṭ is one who precedes.
ZAJJAJ:v3p358/r1.anchor: يقال: قد فرط منه أمر أي قد بدر منه أمر، وقد أفرط في الشيء

ZAJJAJ:v3p358/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p358/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ZAJJAJ:v3p358/r2.claim: The Prophet said, ‘I will precede you at the Pond,’ using faraṭ for one who goes ahead.
ZAJJAJ:v3p358/r2.anchor: ومنه قوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - " أنا فرطكم على الحوض ".

TABRISI:20:52-53/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:52-53/r10.claim: Asmaʿu is a sentence that may serve as a second predicate or be accusative as a circumstantial clause.
TABRISI:20:52-53/r10.anchor: أسمع جملة في موضع الرفع بكونها خبرا بعد خبر

TABRISI:20:52-53/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:52-53/r15.claim: Moses and Aaron feared that Pharaoh would rush to punish them, exceed limits in harming them, or kill them before weighing their proof and reject them in increased disbelief.
TABRISI:20:52-53/r15.anchor: أي نخشى أن يتقدم فينا بعذاب ويعجل علينا

THALABI:v6p246/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p246/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p246/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses and Aaron feared Pharaoh would hurry to kill and punish them.
THALABI:v6p246/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعجل بالقتل والعقوبة

THALABI:v6p246/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p246/r4.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v6p246/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses their fear that Pharaoh would exceed the bounds.

THALABI:v6p246/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p246/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p246/r5.claim: Other interpreters say Pharaoh might overpower them, or that he might become arrogant and defiant.
THALABI:v6p246/r5.anchor: وقيل: يغلبنا أو أن يطغى يتكبر ويستعصي علينا.

STUDYQURAN:20:45/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:45/r1.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:20:45/r1.claim: Their fear that Pharaoh would act hastily is understood as fear that he would hasten their punishment; his swift execution of the sorcerers illustrates this tendency.
STUDYQURAN:20:45/r1.anchor: refers to his hastening their punishment (JJ); for Pharaoh’s tendency to punish swiftly as evidenced by his summary execution of the sorcerers

STUDYQURAN:20:45/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:45/r2.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:20:45/r2.claim: Alternatively, Moses and Aaron feared Pharaoh would kill them before considering the proofs they brought.
STUDYQURAN:20:45/r2.anchor: it can refer to Pharaoh’s killing them without actually pondering over the proofs they would have brought to him (Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:20:45/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:45/r3.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:20:45/r3.claim: Their fear of Pharaoh’s transgression can mean that he would exceed bounds in punishing them.
STUDYQURAN:20:45/r3.anchor: the concern that he would go beyond bounds in punishing them

STUDYQURAN:20:45/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:45/r4.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:20:45/r4.claim: Alternatively, they feared that Pharaoh’s disbelief would increase as he tried to refute them.

TAB-FULL:v16p77/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p77/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p77/r1.claim: Moses and Aaron fear Pharaoh will hurry to punish them if they summon him to the mission God commanded.
TAB-FULL:v16p77/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، {أن يفرط علينا} [طه: 45] قال: عقوبة منه

TAB-FULL:v16p77/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p77/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p77/r2.claim: فرط can describe an act that gets ahead of someone; a فارط is one who goes ahead of a group to water or a stopping place, as the cited rajaz says the foreigner got ahead and hastened upon us.

TAB-FULL:v16p77/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p77/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p77/r3.claim: Al-Tabari distinguishes ifrāṭ, excess and transgression, from tafrīṭ, delay or negligence.
TAB-FULL:v16p77/r3.anchor: وأما الإفراط: فهو الإسراف والإشطاط والتعدي. يقال منه: أفرطت في قولك

TAB-FULL:v16p77/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p77/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p77/r4.claim: Mujahid explains the feared action as punishment from Pharaoh.
TAB-FULL:v16p77/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، {أن يفرط علينا} [طه: 45] قال: عقوبة منه

TAB-FULL:v16p77/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p77/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p77/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says they feared Pharaoh would hasten against them as soon as they conveyed God’s speech or command.
TAB-FULL:v16p77/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {إننا نخاف أن يفرط علينا أو أن يطغى} [طه: 45] قال: نخاف أن يعجل علينا إذ نبلغه كلامك أو أمرك

TABATABAI:20:45/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:45/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:45/r1.claim: If the testing account omitted completion of evidence for the wretched, proof and accountability would fail; without complete proof on either side, it would not take effect.
TABATABAI:20:45/r1.anchor: ولو ألغي التكميل في جانب الشقاء لغى الامتحان فيه، فلم تتم الحجة فيه ولا انقطع العذر،

TABATABAI:20:45/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:45/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:45/r2.claim: Al-faraṭ literally means advancing; contrasted with tyranny here, it means Pharaoh may hasten punishment before the call and miracle are fully presented.
TABATABAI:20:45/r2.anchor: الفرط التقدم والمراد به بقرينة مقابلته الطغيان أن يعجل بالعقوبة

TABATABAI:20:45/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:45/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:45/r3.claim: Tyranny means exceeding limits in oppression, worsening Israelite punishment and daring against the sacred in ways Pharaoh had not dared before the mission.
TABATABAI:20:45/r3.anchor: أن يتجاوز حده في ظلمه فيقابل الدعوة بتشديد عذاب بني إسرائيل

TABATABAI:20:45/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:45/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:45/r4.claim: The fear attributed to Moses and Aaron is unobjectionable in light of the earlier discussion of God's command to Moses to take the staff without fear.
TABATABAI:20:45/r4.anchor: ونسبة الخوف إليهما لا بأس بها كما تقدم الكلام فيها في تفسير قوله تعالى { قال خذها ولا تخف }.

TABATABAI:20:45/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:45/r5.speaker: المعترضون
TABATABAI:20:45/r5.claim: An objection says the earlier promise to strengthen Moses through Aaron and shield both from Pharaoh already gave them security, making their later fear inexplicable.
TABATABAI:20:45/r5.anchor: واستشكل على الآية بأن قوله تعالى في موضع آخر لموسى في جواب سؤاله إشراك أخيه في أمره

TABATABAI:20:46-47/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r8.claim: Their earlier fear was for Moses' own life, as his fear of being killed shows; the fear in this verse concerns the mission and its consequences.
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r8.anchor: والذي في هذه الآية خوف منهما على الدعوة كما تقدم.

TABATABAI:20:46-47/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r9.claim: Alternatively, the verse combines Moses' fear from the earlier private encounter with Aaron's fear after the command reached him; the events need not be one occasion.
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r9.anchor: على أن من الجائز أن يكون هذا الخوف المحكي في الآية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r1.claim: Yafruta means to act hastily against them by punishing them; Ibn Abbas, Mujāhid, exegetes, and linguists agree.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r1.anchor: {قالا ربنا إننا نخاف أن يفرط علينا} أي: يبادر ويعجل بعقوبتنا.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r2.speaker: الكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r2.claim: Al-Kisāʾī gives the forms faraṭa, yafriṭu, furūṭan, faraṭan, and faraṭānan for acting hastily against someone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r2.anchor: وقال الكسائي] (¬6): (يقال: فرط عليهم، يفرط، فروطا، وفرطا، وفرطانا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r3.speaker: الأصمعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r3.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī says faraṭtu al-qawma means I went ahead of the people; from it come al-fāriṭ and the one who reaches water first.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r3.anchor: وقال الأصمعي: (يقال: فرطت القوم، وأنا أفرطهم فرطا إذا تقدمتهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r4.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r4.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī glosses al-faraṭ as haste.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r4.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: (الفرط: العجلة، يقال: فرط يفرط)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r5.claim: The commentary previously discussed this word in its explanation of 16:62.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r5.anchor: وذكرنا هذا الحرف عند قوله: {وأنهم مفرطون} [النحل: 62].

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r6.claim: Here yatghā means to exceed the limit in mistreating Moses and Aaron.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r6.anchor: وقوله تعالى: (أو أن يطغى) أي: يجاوز الحد في الإساءة بنا.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r7.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p410/r7.claim: Al-Kalbī specifies the feared transgression as Pharaoh killing them.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r3.claim: They fear Pharaoh may hasten to kill and punish them.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r4.claim: They also fear he may become arrogant and rebellious.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r6.claim: They fear Pharaoh will rush to punish them and kill them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r6.anchor: {قالا ربنا إننا نخاف أن يفرط علينا} [طه: 45] أن يعجل علينا بالعقوبة يطغى فيقتلنا.

BURHAN:v1p140/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p140/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p140/r6.claim: أو أن, with hamza before waw, occurs in Hud, Bani Israil, Ta Ha, and al-Mumin; examples include Hud and al-Mumin.

ITQAN:v2p343/r25.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p343/r25.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p343/r25.claim: An-yafruṭ means to hasten or act precipitously.

ITQAN:v2p343/r26.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p343/r26.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p343/r26.claim: Yaṭghā means to transgress or overstep.

ITQAN:v1p286/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p286/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p286/r1.claim: Recitation should be beautified and adorned by a good voice, according to reports cited from Ibn Hibban and others; a beautiful voice increases the Qur’an’s beauty.
ITQAN:v1p286/r1.anchor: يسن تحسين الصوت بالقراءة وتزيينها لحديث ابن حبان وغيره

ITQAN:v1p286/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p286/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p286/r2.claim: Those without a naturally beautiful voice should improve it as much as they can, without excessive stretching that distorts recitation.
ITQAN:v1p286/r2.anchor: فإن لم يكن حسن الصوت حسنه ما استطاع بحيث لا يخرج إلى حد التمطيط

ITQAN:v1p286/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p286/r3.speaker: الشافعي
ITQAN:v1p286/r3.claim: Al-Shafiʿi’s Mukhtasar says there is no objection to reciting with melodies; a report from al-Rabiʿ al-Jizi says he disliked it.
ITQAN:v1p286/r3.anchor: وأما القراءة بالألحان فنص الشافعي في المختصر أنه لا بأس بها

ITQAN:v1p286/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p286/r4.speaker: الرافعي
ITQAN:v1p286/r4.claim: Al-Rafiʿi says the jurists do not really differ: dislike applies to excessive elongation, overfilled vowels, or assimilation where it does not belong.
ITQAN:v1p286/r4.anchor: قال الرافعي قال الجمهور ليست على قولين بل المكروه أن يفرط في المد

ITQAN:v1p286/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p286/r5.speaker: النووي
ITQAN:v1p286/r5.claim: Al-Nawawi’s Rawda says this excess is forbidden and makes the reader sinful, with the listener also sinful; he takes this to be what al-Shafiʿi meant by dislike.
ITQAN:v1p286/r5.anchor: والصحيح أن الإفراط على الوجه المذكور حرام يفسق به القارئ ويأثم المستمع

ITQAN:v1p286/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p286/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p286/r6.claim: A report attributed to al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi commands recitation in Arab melodies and warns against the styles of scriptural communities and immoral people, likening later recitation to song and monastic chanting.
ITQAN:v1p286/r6.anchor: اقرؤوا القرآن بلحون العرب وأصواتها وإياكم ولحون أهل الكتابين وأهل الفسق

ITQAN:v1p286/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p286/r7.speaker: النووي
ITQAN:v1p286/r7.claim: Al-Nawawi recommends asking a good-voiced reader to recite and listening to that recitation, based on a sound hadith.
ITQAN:v1p286/r7.anchor: ويستحب طلب القراءة من حسن الصوت والأصغاء إليها للحديث الصحيح

ITQAN:v1p286/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p286/r8.speaker: النووي
ITQAN:v1p286/r8.claim: Al-Nawawi permits group recitation and turns, where one person reads a portion and the next continues with another portion.
ITQAN:v1p286/r8.anchor: ولا بأس باجتماع الجماعة في القراءة ولا بإدارتها

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p398/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p398/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p398/r1.claim: In al-Mutanabbī’s line, the source noun should be annexed to the object to deny that the fingers preserve anything; the transmitted construction instead attributes preservation to them.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p398/r1.anchor: وإضافته الحفظ إلى ضميرها في قوله : ما حفظها الأشياء ، يقتضي أن يكون قد أثبت لها حفظا .

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p398/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p398/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p398/r2.claim: Unlike a verb construction such as saying it is not someone’s habit to preserve things, annexing a verbal noun to its agent asserts that the action occurred.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p398/r2.anchor: ذاك أن إضافة المصدر إلى الفاعل يقتضي وجوده ، وأنه قد كان منه . يبين ذلك

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p398/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p398/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p398/r3.claim: The idiom لا تضجر ضجر زيد presents Zayd as actually becoming angry, at least making anger a habitual feature, rather than denying that it occurs.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p398/r3.anchor: كنت قد جعلت زيدا يضجر ضربا من الضجر مثل أن تجعله يفرط فيه

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p279#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p279#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p279#3/r1.claim: Yafruṭ means to hurry ahead or act first; farṭ is precedence and going ahead.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p279#3/r1.anchor: {نخاف أن يفرط علينا} أي: يعجل ويقدم. والفرط: التقدم والسبق.

SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r1.claim: أن يفرط is the object of نخاف.
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r1.anchor: قوله: { أن يفرط }: " أن يفرط " مفعول " نخاف ".

SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r2.claim: فرط means to precede; a فارط goes ahead of those coming to water, and فرس فرط outruns horses, so they fear Pharaoh will hasten to punish them.
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r2.anchor: ويقال: فرط يفرط: سبق وتقدم، ومنه الفارط. وهو الذي يتقدم الورادة إلى الماء وفرس فرط: يسبق الخيل،

SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r3.claim: An anonymous poetic line's فراط لوراد and the hadith أنا فرطكم على الحوض illustrate a forerunner who goes ahead of others to the water or basin.
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث: " أنا فرطكم على الحوض " أي: سابقكم ومتقدمكم.

SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r4.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب وابن محيصن وأبو نوفل
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r4.claim: These readers use the passive يفرط; the fear is that Pharaoh be driven to punish them hastily by his people, ambition, or claim to divinity.
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r4.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب وابن محيصن وأبو نوفل " يفرط " بضم حرف المضارعة وفتح الراء على البناء للمفعول

SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r5.speaker: ابن محيصن والزعفراني
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r5.claim: In one transmission Ibn Muhaysin and al-Zaʿfarani read with a prefixed ḍamma and kasra on rāʾ, from أفرط; al-Zamakhshari explains that someone may drive Pharaoh to hurry.
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن في رواية والزعفراني " أن يفرط " بضم حرف المضارعة وكسر الراء من أفرط.

SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r6.speaker: كعب بن زهير
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r6.claim: Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr's verse uses أفرطه for getting to a water vessel ahead of time and filling it with white cloudlike rain.
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r6.anchor:
قال كعب ابن زهير.
3293 تنفي الرياح القذى عنه وأفرطه

SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r7.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r7.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows an omitted subject, 'a statement from him might get ahead of us,' or Pharaoh as the subject, as in يطغى.
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r7.anchor: وجعله أبو البقاء مضمرا لدلالة الكلام عليه فقال " فيجوز أن يكون التقدير: أن يفرط علينا منه قول،

SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r8.claim: The author favors Pharaoh as the subject of يفرط as the evident reading that should not be abandoned.
SAMIN-DURR:20:45/r8.anchor: وفاعل " يفرط " ضمير فرعون. وهذا هو الظاهر الذي ينبغي أن لا يعدل عنه

ASAD-NOTES:20:45#n29/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:45#n29/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:45#n29/r1.claim: The brothers fear Pharaoh might banish or kill them outright, preventing them from fully delivering God's message.
ASAD-NOTES:20:45#n29/r1.anchor: lest he prevent us, by banishing or killing us outright, from delivering Thy message fully

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#2/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#2/r7.claim: Another possible reason for hearing before sight is its shorter range: hearing ordinarily suggests nearness, so God's promise to hear and see Moses and Aaron conveys closeness.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#2/r7.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون تقديم السمع على البصر لسبب آخر عدا الأفضلية، وهو أن مدى السمع أقل من مدى الرؤية

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r2.claim: Ta-Ha presents a joint mission: both are sent, answer in fear, receive reassurance, deliver the message, and are addressed by Pharaoh together, making Aaron Moses's partner in conveying the message.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r2.anchor: فقد أمر كلاً من موسى وهرون بالذهاب بآياته

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p31/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p31/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p31/r2.claim: The author favors hearing’s importance for receiving revelation: a blind person can understand a message, while a deaf person is harder to inform; prophets were not deaf, though one could be blind.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p31/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن السمع بالنسبة إلى تلقي الرسالة أفضل

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p31/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p31/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p31/r3.claim: Hearing may also precede sight because its range is shorter; in God’s assurance to Moses and Aaron, “I hear” suggests nearness, unlike seeing from afar.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p31/r3.anchor: مدى السمع أقل من مدى الرؤية فقدم ذا المدى الأقل متدرجاً من القصر إلى الطول في المدى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p482/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p482/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p482/r3.claim: He offers another ordering rationale: hearing has shorter range than sight, so it comes first; hearing also evokes nearness, while seeing can extend farther.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p482/r3.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون تقديم السمع على البصر لسبب آخر عدا الأفضلية وهو أن مدى السمع أقل من مدى الرؤية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r1.claim: قالا begins an explanatory resumption answering the implied question of what Moses and Aaron said after receiving the command.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r1.anchor: استئناف بيانى كأنه قيل : فماذا قالا حين امرا بما امرا فقيل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r2.claim: If Aaron was absent, plural attribution includes him by grammatical predominance; alternatively he spoke after reuniting with Moses and their words are combined in the revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r2.anchor: وأسند القول اليهما مع أن القائل هو موسى عليه السلام على القول بغيبة هرون عليه السلام للتغليب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r3.claim: The plural report may also mean both spoke together at Sinai; al-Alusi compares it with the plural address to messengers in 23:51, though they were not each addressed individually.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r3.anchor: وجوز كونهما مجتمعين عند الطور وقالا جميعا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r4.claim: The apparent meaning is that Pharaoh may hasten to punish them before they complete the invitation and display the miracle; فرط denotes going ahead.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r4.anchor: أي أن يجعل علينا بالعقوبة ولا يصبر إلى اتمام الدعوة واظهار المعجزة من فرط إذا تقدم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows an omitted noun: they fear that a statement from Pharaoh will issue against them; al-Alusi regards this as contrary to the apparent sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r5.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء : يجوز أن يكون التقدير أن يفرط علينا منه قول فاضمر القول

ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r6.speaker: يحيى وأبو نوفل وابن محيصن
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r6.claim: Yahya, Abu Nawfal, and Ibn Muhaysin read يفرط with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the rāʾ, from form IV, meaning Pharaoh is driven to hurry.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r6.anchor: وقرا يحيى وابو نوفل وابن محيصن في رواية ( يفرط ) بضم الياء وفتح الراء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r7.speaker: فرقة والزعفرانى عن ابن محيصن
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r7.claim: Another group and al-Zaʿfarani from Ibn Muhaysin read يفرط with kasra on the rāʾ, deriving it from excess in causing harm.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r7.anchor: وقرأت فرقة والزعفرانى عن ابن محيصن ( يفرط ) بضم الياء وكسر الراء من الافراط

ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r8.claim: The fear appears to conflict with God's promise that Pharaoh would not reach them; the phrase may mean he cannot defeat them in argument, and the timing of the promise is uncertain, though early authorities support the apparent sense of physical harm.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r8.anchor: واستشكل هذا القول مع قوله تعالى : ( سنشد عضدك باخيك ونجعل لكما سلطانا فلا يصلون اليكما )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r9.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r9.claim: The Imam says Moses and Aaron knew rationally nothing would interrupt their delivery, but asked for added reassurance from transmitted revelation, as Abraham asked to see how God revives the dead; al-Alusi rejects the certainty claim as unjustified.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r9.anchor: وزعم الأمام أنهما قد آمنا وقوع ما يقطعهما عن الاداء بالدليل العقلى إلا أنهما طلبا بما ذكر ما يزيد في ثبات قلوبهما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r10.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r10.claim: The Imam distinguishes Moses' requested expansion of the chest as capacity to retain commandments and law without error, rather than freedom from fear; al-Alusi notes many exegetes interpret it as inner ease and patience under hardship.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r10.anchor: بأن شرح الصدر عبارة عن قوته على ضبط تلك الأوامر والنواهى وحفظ تلك الشرائع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r11.claim: Fear of hardship does not conflict with meeting it patiently and without distress; people can seek protection from an affliction and endure it steadfastly if it arrives.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r11.anchor: لا منافاة بين الخوف من شئ والصبر عليه وعدم الضجر منه إذا وقع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r12.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r12.claim: Another explanation says they feared punishment only because it would interrupt their hoped-for delivery and guidance, not for themselves; asking specifically for removal of this obstacle reinforces Moses' earlier general request for help.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r12.anchor: أنهما عليهما السلام لم يخافا من العقوبة إلا لقطعها الأداء المرجو به الهداية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r13.claim: The plural may also reflect Aaron's inclusion even though the passage has not previously stated that he was assured of protection.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r13.anchor: وقيل : أن في الآية تغليبا منه لاخيه هرون على نفسه عليهما السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r14.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r14.claim: The Imam argues that delay after repeated commands would imply prophetic disobedience only if commands require immediate action; he treats this as strong evidence that an imperative does not itself entail immediacy.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196#2/r14.anchor: واجاب الأمام بأن الدلالة مسلمة لو دل الأمر على الفور وليس فليس ثم قال : وهذا من اقوى الدلائل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p197/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197/r1.claim: أو prevents excluding the two possibilities; Pharaoh may grow still more tyrannical and say something irreverent with audacity and harshness.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197/r1.anchor: لمنع الخلو والمراد أو أن يزداد طغيانا إلى أن يقول في شأنك ما لا ينبغى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p197/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197/r2.claim: The explicit أن, though not needed for the sense, signals special concern and conveys that they fear both alternatives as actual possibilities.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197/r2.anchor: واظهار كلمة أن مع سداد المعنى بدونه لاظهار كمال الاعتناء بالأمر والأشعار بتحقق الخوف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains yafruta as Pharaoh hurrying to kill or punish them; the verb can mean hastening harm, while faraṭa minhu describes something that came suddenly or ahead.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: يعجل علينا بالقتل والعقوبة، يقال: فرط عليه فلان إذا عجل بمكروه، وفرط منه أمر أي بدر وسبق،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276/r2.claim: They fear that Pharaoh may exceed the bounds in mistreating them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276/r2.anchor: {أو أن يطغى} أي يجاوز الحد في الإساءة إلينا.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:45/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:45/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:45/r1.claim: They fear Pharaoh will hasten to punish them before their mission is completed and the miracle shown; فرط means to go ahead, as in a forerunner or a horse that outruns others.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:45/r1.anchor: أن يعجل علينا بالعقوبة ولا يصبر إلى تمام الدعوة وإظهار المعجزة

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:45/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:45/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:45/r2.claim: A reading from أفرطته means someone incites Pharaoh to haste, whether arrogance, fear for his rule, or a human or jinn devil; another reading means excess in harming them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:45/r2.anchor: وقرىء { يفرط } من أفرطته إذا حملته على العجلة

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:45/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:45/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:45/r3.claim: They also fear Pharaoh will grow more tyrannical and, through insolence and harshness, say what is improper of God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:45/r3.anchor: أو أن يزداد طغيانا فيتخطى إلى أن يقول فيك ما لا ينبغي

BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r1.claim: Because Pharaoh was extremely powerful, Moses and Aaron felt they could be destroyed unless God protected them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r1.anchor: ولما كان فرعون في غاية الجبروت

BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r2.claim: The added nūn intensifies their fear and complaint so that reassurance can answer their distress in proportion to it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r2.anchor: بإظهار النونالثالثة إبلاغا في إظهار الشكوى

BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r3.claim: Yafruta means Pharaoh might hasten to punish them before they finish conveying the message, like someone leaping toward a thing.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r3.anchor: بالعقوبة قبل إتمام البلاغ عجلة من يطفر ويثب إلى الشيء

BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r4.claim: They also fear that Pharaoh will exceed his current arrogance and go further in transgression.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r4.anchor: فيتجاوز إلى أعظم مما هو فيه من الاستكبار

DURR-FULL:v5p580/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains yafruta as Pharaoh hastening against them and yaṭghā as his transgressing.
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {إننا نخاف أن يفرط علينا} قال: يعجل {أو أن يطغى} قال: يعتدي

DURR-FULL:v5p580/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r4.claim: Mujāhid says Moses and Aaron feared punishment from Pharaoh.
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {إننا نخاف أن يفرط علينا أو أن يطغى} قال: عقوبة منه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r1.claim: After showing Moses the two signs, God gives him the daunting mission of confronting the earth's mightiest ruler; the next verses recount Moses and Aaron's fear and God's reassurance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r1.anchor: لما أظهر الله له الآيتين فعلم بذلك أنه مؤيد من الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r11.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r11.claim: The majority read يفرط with fatḥa on yāʾ and ḍamma on rāʾ, meaning Pharaoh may hasten to harm them, from the one who goes ahead to water.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «يفرط» بفتح الياء وضم الراء ومعناه يعجل ويسرع بمكروه فينا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r12.speaker: القطامي عمير بن شييم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r12.claim: Al-Qutami's verse compares people who hurried to the first arrivals at a watering place, illustrating the sense of one who goes ahead.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r12.anchor: ومنه فارط في الماء وهو الذي يتقدم القوم إليه قال الشاعر القطامي عمير بن شييم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r13.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r13.claim: One group reads يُفَرِّط with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on rāʾ, meaning Pharaoh may be extreme in harming them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r13.anchor: وقالت فرقة «يفرط» بضم الياء وكسر الراء ومعناه يشتط في إذايتنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r14.speaker: ابن محيصن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r14.claim: Ibn Muhaysin reads يفرط with ḍamma on yāʾ and fatḥa on rāʾ, meaning an agent may drive him to rush against them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r14.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن «يفرط» بضم الياء وفتح الراء ومعناها أن يحمله حامل على التسرع إلينا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r1.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r1.claim: The commentators say Aaron was then absent in Egypt; God told him to meet Moses, and after they met Moses told him of the mission and his request for Aaron's help.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون كان هارون يؤمئذ غائبا بمصر فأوحى الله تعالى إلى هارون أن يتلقى موسى فتلقاه على مرحلة فقال له موسى إن الله تعالى أمرني أن آتي فرعون فسألته أن يجعلك معي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbari allows that Moses alone spoke, with dual wording because Aaron was joined to him; Arabic can address one person with dual forms.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r2.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري ويجوز أن يكون القائل لذلك موسى وحده واخبر الله عنه بالتثنية لما ضم اليه هارون فان العرب قد توقع التثنية على الواحد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو وابن السميفع وابن يعمر وأبو العالية
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r3.claim: These readers use yufriṭ, with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on rāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r3.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن عمرو وابن السميفع وابن يعمر وأبو العالية أن يفرط برفع الياء وكسر الراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r4.speaker: عكرمة وإبراهيم النخعي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r4.claim: ʿIkrima and Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi read yafruṭ, with fatḥa on yāʾ and rāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r4.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة وإبراهيم النخعي أن يفرط بفتح الياء والراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r5.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي وابن محيصن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r5.claim: Abu Rajaʾ al-ʿUtaridi and Ibn Muhaysin read yufarraṭ, with ḍamma on yāʾ and fatḥa on rāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء العطاردي وابن محيصن أن يفرط برفع الياء وفتح الراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the fear as Pharaoh rushing to punish them; related forms indicate something coming early, excess, or falling short, all rooted in going ahead.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج المعنى أن يبادر بعقوبتنا يقال قد فرط منه أمر أي قد بدر وقد أفرط في الشيء إذا اشتط فيه وفرط في الشيء إذا قصر ومعناه كله التقدم في الشيء لأن الفرط في اللغة المتقدم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r7.claim: The Prophet said, “I precede you at the Pool,” using faraṭ for one who goes ahead.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r7.anchor: ومنه قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام أنا فرطكم على الحوض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r8.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r8.claim: One interpretation of their fear is that Pharaoh would become defiant and unmanageable.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says they feared Pharaoh would exceed bounds in harming them and attack before they could deliver God's words and command.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p289/r9.anchor: والثاني يجاوز الحد في الإساءة الينا قال ابن زيد نخاف أن يعجل علينا قبل أن نبلغه كلامك وأمرك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r1.claim: Moses and Aaron sought God's protection, fearing Pharaoh might hasten to punish them or attack them unjustly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r1.anchor: يعنيان أن يبدر إليهما بعقوبة، أو يعتدي عليهما فيعاقبهما وهما لا يستحقان منه ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r2.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd glosses “يَفْرُط” as “he hastens.”
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r2.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن بن زيد: {أن يفرط} يعجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r3.claim: Mujahid explains “يَفْرُط” as Pharaoh extending his violence against them.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak, reporting from Ibn Abbas, glosses “يَطْغى” as transgressing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r4.anchor: وقال الضحاك، عن ابن عباس: {أو أن يطغى} : يعتدي

JISHUMI:v7p4666/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4666/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4666/r10.claim: Ifrāṭ means excess and tafrīṭ means shortcoming; the root concerns going ahead, as in a forerunner arriving at water.
JISHUMI:v7p4666/r10.anchor: والإفراط: الإسراف، والتفريط: التقصير، وأصل الباب: التقدم، ومنه الفارط: المتقدم أمام القوم إلى الماء

JISHUMI:v7p4666/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4666/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4666/r11.claim: Farṭ is advancing where one should not or delaying where one should advance; extravagance thus rushes away from the truth.
JISHUMI:v7p4666/r11.anchor: والفرط تقدم فيما ينبغي ألا يقدم، أو تأخر فيما يجب التقدم له، ومنه: أنا فرطكم على الحوض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r1.claim: Faraṭa means to precede or get ahead; al-fāriṭ reaches the watering place first, and a faras faraṭ is a horse that outruns others.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r1.anchor: فرط : سبق وتقدم . ومنه الفارط : الذي يتقدم الواردة . وفرس فرط : يسبق الخيل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r2.claim: On the basic reading, Moses and Aaron fear Pharaoh will hurry to punish them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r2.anchor: أي : نخاف أن يعجل علينا بالعقوبة ويبادرنا بها .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r3.claim: Another reading derives yufriṭ from a causative verb: they fear that some force will drive Pharaoh to act hastily.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r3.anchor: وقرىء ( يفرط ) من أفرطه غيره إذا حمله على العجلة .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r4.claim: The force prompting haste could be Satan, Pharaoh’s arrogance and claim to divinity, his love of rule, or rebellious Coptic courtiers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r4.anchor: خافا أن يحمله حامل على المعاجلة بالعقاب من شيطان ، أو من جبروته واستكباره وادعائه بالربوبية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r5.claim: A further reading takes the verb from excess in harm: they fear Pharaoh will abruptly block their delivery of the message.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r5.anchor: وقرىء ( يفرط ) من الإفراط في الأذية ، أي : نخاف أن يحول بيننا وبين تبليغ الرسالة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r6.claim: Alternatively, Pharaoh might exceed bounds in punishing them, given his known viciousness and arrogance.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r6.anchor: أو يجاوز الحد في معاقبتنا إن لم يعاجل ، بناء على ما عرفا وجربا من شرارته وعتوه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r7.claim: The unqualified, allusive “or transgress” politely avoids openly voicing the enormity Pharaoh might commit against God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67/r7.anchor: بالتخطي إلى أن يقول فيك ما لا ينبغي ، لجرأته عليك وقسوة قلبه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405/r1.claim: One interpretation is that Pharaoh might hurry against them; a rajaz line glosses the verb with hastening.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405/r1.anchor: أن يعجل علينا , قال الراجز : قد أفرط العلج علينا وعجل

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405/r2.speaker: المبرد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad explains it as punishing them like someone excessive in sin; in usage, الإفراط is excess and التفريط is shortcoming.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405/r2.anchor: يعذبنا عذاب الفارط في الذنب , وهو المتقدم فيه , قاله المبرد ويقال لمن أكثر في الشيء أفرط

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p405/r3.claim: The feared transgression is that Pharaoh might kill them.

MUJAHID:v1p397#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p397#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p397#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says Moses and Aaron feared that Pharaoh would punish them hastily.
MUJAHID:v1p397#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ نخاف أن يفرط علينا ﴾ يقول يفرط علينا فرعون عقوبة

MUJAHID:v1p398#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p398#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p398#4/r1.claim: Mujahid says they feared Pharaoh would hasten punishment against them.
MUJAHID:v1p398#4/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ نخاف أن يفرط علينا ﴾ فرعون عقوبة

MUQATIL:20:41-45/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:41-45/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:41-45/r8.claim: Moses and Aaron fear Pharaoh will hasten to kill them or become obstinate.
MUQATIL:20:41-45/r8.anchor: قالا ربنا إننا نخاف أن يفرط علينا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#2/r1.claim: Yafruṭa means to hasten punishment; fāriṭ and faraṭa ʿalayhi convey haste.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#2/r1.anchor: يعجل علينا بالعقوبة ومنه ألفارط يقال فرط عليه أي عجل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#2/r2.claim: They fear Pharaoh will overstep bounds in mistreating them.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r1.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says yafruta means hasten and yaṭghā means aggress.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r1.anchor: قال الضحاك: { يفرط } يعجل. قال: و { يطغى } يعتدي.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r2.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r2.claim: Al-Naḥḥās supplies an omitted noun: they fear an act from Pharaoh will hasten against them.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r2.anchor: النحاس: التقدير نخاف أن يفرط علينا منه أمر،

QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r3.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains فرط منه أمر as something springing forth, أفرط as excess, and فرط as leaving or neglecting.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r3.anchor: قال الفراء: فرط منه أمر أي بدر قال: وأفرط أسرف. قال: وفرط ترك.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r4.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r4.claim: The majority read yafruṭ with fatḥa on yāʾ and ḍamma on rāʾ, meaning Pharaoh may rush to punish them.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r4.anchor: وقراءة الجمهور «يفرط» بفتح الياء وضم الراء، ومعناه يعجل ويبادر بعقوبتنا.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r5.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad explains the fear as Pharaoh punishing them for a supposed prior sin, as one already ahead in wrongdoing.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r5.anchor: أي يعذبنا عذاب الفارط في الذنب وهو المتقدم فيه قاله المبرد.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r6.speaker: ابن محيصن
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r6.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin also reads yafrata with fatḥa on both yāʾ and rāʾ; al-Mahdawī suggests it may be a dialect.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r6.anchor: وقرأت فرقة منهم ابن محيصن «يفرط» بفتح الياء والراء قال المهدوي: ولعلها لغة.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r7.speaker: ابن محيصن
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r7.claim: Another Ibn Muḥayṣin reading has ḍamma on yāʾ and fatḥa on rāʾ, meaning someone may drive Pharaoh to rush against them.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r7.anchor: وعنه أيضا بضم الياء وفتح الراء ومعناها أن يحمله حامل على التسرع إلينا.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r8.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة وابن محيصن
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, and Ibn Muḥayṣin read yufriṭ with ḍamma yāʾ and kasra rāʾ, meaning Pharaoh may go too far in harm; the cited rajaz witnesses this.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r8.anchor: وقرأت طائفة «يفرط» بضم الياء وكسر الراء وبها قرأ ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة وابن محيصن أيضا.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r9.speaker: الراجز
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r9.claim: The rajaz line uses أفرط for exceeding bounds against people and hurrying.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:45/r9.anchor: ومعناه يشطط في أذيتنا قال الراجز: قد أفرط العلج علينا وعجل

BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r1.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r1.claim: Al-Irshād says the plural speech is by grammatical predominance: Moses is primary in every word and deed, while Aaron follows him.
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r1.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" أسند القول إليهما مع أن القائل حقيقة هو موسى

BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r2.claim: A report says Moses traveled from the mountain toward Egypt alone, without knowing the route and without provisions, mount, or companion; he lived on sparse fruit and game until reaching Egypt.
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r2.anchor: وروي أن موسى انطلق من الطور إلى جانب مصر لا علم له بالطريق

BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r3.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r3.claim: Kāshifī says revelation sent Aaron to meet Moses on the road; after hearing the story, Aaron warned of Pharaoh's power and readiness to kill or crucify, making the brothers apprehensive and prayerful.
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r3.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (ون بمصر توجه فرمود وحى آمد بهارون

BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r4.claim: Fear expects harm based on a likely or known sign, unlike hope, which expects something desired; fear contrasts with security and applies to worldly and next-worldly matters.
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r4.anchor: الخوف توقع مكروه عن إمارة مظنونة أو معلومة كما أن الرجاء

BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r5.claim: Fear of God here means restraining oneself from sins and choosing obedience, rather than bodily terror before a lion.
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r5.anchor: والخوف من الله يراد به ما يخطر بالبال من الرعب كاستشعار الخوف

BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r6.claim: The verb derives from going ahead; a farit prepares a water vessel, so the phrase means Pharaoh may hasten to punish them before the mission and sign are complete.
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r6.anchor: من فرط إذا تقدم تقدما بالقصد ومنه الفارط إلى الماء

BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r7.claim: A variant reading derives the verb from ifrāṭ, meaning excess in causing harm.
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r7.anchor: وقرىء يفرط من الإفراط في الأذية

BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r8.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r8.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya says fear is rooted in human nature even in prophets; Moses and Aaron fear not death itself but failing in servitude by being prevented from delivering the message, while Pharaoh may rebel and insult God's commands.
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r8.anchor: كما في "التأويلات النجمية" يشير إلى أن الخوف مركوز في جبلة الإنسان

BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r9.claim: Pharaoh may grow tyrannical and say what is unfitting about God; the wording courteously says in God's regard rather than against Him, and leaves the greater offense to the end.
BURSEVI:v5p299#2/r9.anchor: أي : يزداد طغيانا إلى أن يقول في شأنك ما لا ينبغي

BURSEVI:v5p300/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p300/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p300/r1.claim: Bursevī also allows that Pharaoh may tyrannize against Moses and Aaron; the preposition is omitted for the verse ending, as the object is omitted in another verse for cadence.
BURSEVI:v5p300/r1.anchor: يقول الفقير : يجوز أن يكون المراد يطغى علينا أي : يجاوز الحد في الإساءة إلينا

RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r1.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r1.claim: Al-Qaffāl addresses the dual address although Aaron was absent: God spoke to Moses, whose leadership included Aaron, and the dual speech is hypothetical; scripture uses similar collective attribution.
RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r1.anchor: أن الكلام كان مع موسى عليه السلام وحده إلا أنه كان متبوع هارون فجعل الخطاب معه خطابا مع هارون وكلام هارون على سبيل التقدير

RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r2.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r2.claim: Alternatively, Moses may have paused after God granted his request until he met Aaron, after which God addressed them both.
RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r2.anchor: يحتمل أن الله تعالى لما قال : { قد أوتيت سؤلك ياموسى * موسى } سكت حتى لقي أخاه

RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود وحفصة
RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r3.claim: A reading attributed to the codices of Ibn Masʿūd and Ḥafṣa has the singular “he said,” with Moses speaking for himself and his brother.
RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r3.anchor: أنه في مصحف ابن مسعود وحفصة : { قال ربنا * إننا نخاف } أي قال موسى : أنا وأخي نخاف فرعون

RAZI-FULL:v22p52#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p52#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p52#2/r1.claim: The question of plural speech despite Aaron’s absence is repeated here; Rāzī refers back to the answer already given.
RAZI-FULL:v22p52#2/r1.anchor: قوله : { قالا ربنا } يدل على أن المتكلم بذلك موسى وهرون عليهما السلام وهرون لم يكن حاضرا هذا المقال فكيف ذلك وجوابه قد تقدم

RAZI-FULL:v22p52#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p52#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p52#2/r2.claim: An expanded breast means strength to retain and preserve commands and laws without forgetfulness or distortion; it does not mean freedom from fear.
RAZI-FULL:v22p52#2/r2.anchor: شرح الصدر عبارة عن تقويته على ضبط تلك الأوامر والنواحي وحفظ تلك الشرائع على وجه لا يتطرق إليه السهو والتحريف

RAZI-FULL:v22p52#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p52#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p52#2/r3.claim: Moses and Aaron trusted that Pharaoh would not kill them, but feared harm before completing the mission or after delivery.
RAZI-FULL:v22p52#2/r3.anchor: قد أمنا ذلك وإن جوزا أن ينالهما السوء من قبل تمام الأداء أو بعده

RAZI-FULL:v22p52#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p52#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p52#2/r4.claim: They also sought further firmness in calling Pharaoh, adding revealed assurance to rational evidence for greater tranquility, as Abraham asked in 2:260.
RAZI-FULL:v22p52#2/r4.anchor: استظهرا بأن سألا ربهما ما يزيد في ثبات قلبهما على دعائه وذلك بأن ينضاف الدليل النقلي إلى العقلي زيادة في الطمأنينة

RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r1.claim: If commands required immediate action, their delay to express fear would strongly imply disobedience; since prophetic disobedience is excluded, this supports the principle that a command does not itself require immediacy.
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r1.anchor: لو اقتضى الأمر الفور لكان ذلك من أقوى الدلائل على المعصية لا سيما وقد أكثر الله تعالى من أنواع التشريف

RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r2.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r2.claim: One reading of yafruṭ derives it from going ahead: they feared Pharaoh might hurry to punish them.
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r2.anchor: فرط سبق وتقدم ومنه الفارط الذي يتقدم الواردة وفرس فرط يسبق الخيل والمعنى نخاف أن يعجل علينا بالعقوبة

RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r3.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r3.claim: Another derives it from making someone hasten: they feared Satan, Pharaoh’s claim to divinity or love of rule, or his rebellious Egyptian people might spur him to punish them.
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r3.anchor: أنه مأخوذ من أفرط غيره إذا حمله على العجلة فكان موسى وهارون عليهما السلام خافا من أن يحمله حامل على المعاجلة بالعقوبة

RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r4.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r4.claim: A third takes the word as excessive injury.

RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r5.claim: They feared Pharaoh would transgress by daring to say what is improper about God.
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r5.anchor: المعنى يطغى بالتخطي إلى أن يقول فيك ما لا ينبغي لجراءته عليك

RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r6.claim: The stronger concern is placed last: like the hoopoe ending its excuse with the people’s sun worship, Moses ends with Pharaoh’s offense against God, graver than harm to the messengers.
